title: Referrals and repeat work from existing clients for Medical equipment cleaning (external only)
audience: Solo operators and team owners who clean external medical equipment for clinics and care settings and want repeat batches and referrals from the facility contacts they already serve.
learningOutcomes: Plan a review or referral request, made to the facility contact after the batch is confirmed, that the contact can decline easily.
Write a next-batch offer for a facility with a date, a scope and a price approach, and schedule the check-in that follows it.
Write referral reward terms, including the payment condition and any facility gift rule, before any referral is made.

instruction.heading: Ask the facility contact once the batch is confirmed
instruction.body: The best time to ask for a review or referral is after the facility contact has confirmed that the batch is right, usually at sign-off or when the invoice is paid. Ask in one sentence, name the next step, and make it easy to decline. Sending a review link or QR code is allowed, and Google provides one for this purpose. Do not write reviews for anyone or invent them. Asking only satisfied contacts is called review gating, which a vendor source says Google treats as a violation. One experiment found that a late reminder brought in more reviews than an immediate one, with 2.16 per cent of customers reviewing after a late reminder against 1.32 per cent with no reminder (Baylor Keller Center, 2024); that was one study and not a study of equipment cleaning. The ACCC says incentives for reviews must be disclosed and must not depend on what the review says, and Google bans discounts or goods in exchange for reviews, so check each platform's terms before offering any incentive. Do not ask patients or staff for reviews unless the facility's policy allows it.

instruction.heading: Offer the next batch in writing before the contact leaves
instruction.body: Repeat work is a dependable source of growth for a small service business. At sign-off, propose the next batch with a date: the next external clean of the facility's list, or a clean before a visit or audit the facility tells you about. Put the item list, the interval and the price approach in writing, and confirm that the contact agrees before you change any schedule. If the written offer goes by email or text, check the electronic message rules first. ACMA's guidance indicates that inferred consent is narrow and does not cover a message sent just after a purchase. The research found no source on intervals for equipment cleaning, so the facility's own schedule sets the interval.

instruction.heading: Check in at an interval that suits the service
instruction.body: For a clean or a repair, about ninety days is a starting point to test, not a benchmark. For external equipment work the interval should follow the facility's own schedule. The check asks whether the result still holds, whether anything has changed and whether there is other work to quote. Keep it short and factual. If the check goes by email or text, it can be a commercial message when it promotes any service, even when it is framed as a reminder (Clayton Utz, 9 November 2023).

instruction.heading: Re-contact previous contacts before their busy periods
instruction.body: Plan a short message a few weeks before any period the facility names as busy. Do not assume a busy period the facility has not named. Offer the slots you can deliver, on written terms, with a clear way to opt out. Do not use the message to pressure anyone, and do not contact a contact who has asked not to hear from you. ACMA's guidance says an unsubscribe must be honoured within five working days, so record each opt-out as soon as you receive it and stop sending to that contact.

instruction.heading: Set referral rewards in writing before anyone refers
instruction.body: A referral reward works best when the referrer knows the terms before they refer someone. Decide what you will offer, write down the condition for payment (normally that the referred facility has completed a paid batch), and give the referrer a copy. Research on referral programmes found that stating the referrer's reward in the invitation increased referring across seven studies (Xu, Yu and Tu, 2023), so say what the reward is in the invitation. Get the referred person's consent before a referral message is sent, because the referrer's word alone may not be enough (Clayton Utz, 2017, older source). The research found no source on referrals in this sector. Facility gift and conflict-of-interest policies may apply to rewards offered to clinic or care staff, and the research has no source for those rules, so check the facility's policy before offering anything. Check any cash-based reward, and its tax or contract effect, with an adviser.

procedure: After each batch is signed off, make one review or referral request to the facility contact, and record what was asked and the answer.
Write the next-batch offer with a date, scope, interval and price approach, and confirm it with the contact.
Schedule the check-in for the interval that suits the service, and send it using the electronic message rules.
Plan a re-contact message for each period the facility names, and exclude anyone who has opted out.
Write the referral reward terms and the payment condition before the first referral is made, and check the facility's gift policy.
When a referral books, confirm the referred batch is paid before applying the reward, and record the outcome.
Review at the end of each season which requests, offers and timings produced repeat work.

workedExamples.situation: A clinic manager is happy with the external cleaning and offers to recommend the owner to a care home in the same group. The owner wants to offer a credit on the clinic's next batch if the care home books.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should the owner write down before the care home books, and what should be avoided?
workedExamples.reasoning: The owner writes down the credit, the payment condition (the care home completes a paid batch), the date the credit applies and a copy for the clinic manager. The clinic manager passes on the care home's contact details, and the owner contacts the care home only if its manager agrees. The owner checks the group's gift and conflict policy, because the research has no source for those rules. The owner does not promise a reward he has not written down, does not invent or request a review, and does not take on work outside his licence or insurance.

equipmentAndPpe: Client record with the sign-off date and the review or referral request made
Next-batch offer template with item scope, interval and price approach
Calendar of re-contact dates set by the facility or by the service
No PPE is needed for client follow-up; any site visit follows the site's own safety and infection-control rules

commonErrors.error: Asking for a review before the contact has confirmed the batch is right.
commonErrors.prevention: Ask after sign-off or payment, when the contact has confirmed the result is right.

commonErrors.error: Offering a referral reward that was never written down, so the terms are disputed later.
commonErrors.prevention: Write the reward and its payment condition before any referral is made, and give the referrer a copy.

commonErrors.error: Publishing a facility's, staff member's or patient's name, photo or review without consent for that use.
commonErrors.prevention: Get consent for each thing you plan to publish, and keep the record.

commonErrors.error: Contacting a contact who asked not to hear from you, or using a re-contact message to pressure them.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep an opt-out list, honour it at once, and keep re-contact messages factual and optional.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Publishing a facility's, client's or staff member's name, photo, review or site detail needs consent for that use. Do not write reviews on anyone's behalf. Whether the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) applies to your business is unconfirmed in the research; check the OAIC's small business guidance before relying on it.

Review platforms and referral programmes can have their own rules on incentives. Google bans discounts or goods in exchange for reviews. The ACCC's guidance on online reviews says incentives must be disclosed and must not depend on the review's content. Check each platform's rules before offering any reward.

Check-in and re-contact messages sent by email or text can be commercial electronic messages under the Spam Act 2003 (Cth). A message that promotes any service can be commercial even when it is framed as a service reminder, and ACMA has been enforcing this area, so check each message before sending.

A referral does not extend the licence or authority of the business that accepts the work. Accept only the work your licence and insurance cover, in the state or territory where the work is done, and check the rules for each state. The research did not cover any licence or registration for external equipment cleaning. This lesson does not grant any licence.

qualityStandard: Every review or referral request is made after sign-off or payment, and it includes an easy way to decline.
Every next-batch offer is written, has a date and is confirmed by the contact before the schedule changes.
Every referral reward has written terms and a payment condition, and is paid only when that condition is met.
documentationEvidence: Review or referral request log with the date sent and the answer.
Next-batch offers with the date, scope, interval and contact confirmation.
Referral reward terms with the referral record and payment outcome.
summary: Ask for reviews and referrals after the contact has confirmed the batch, and make it easy to say no.
Offer the next batch in writing, with a date, before the contact leaves.
Set referral rewards and their payment conditions in writing before anyone refers.

knowledgeChecks.question: When is the best time to ask a facility contact for a review or referral?
options: Before the batch starts, so the contact feels committed
After the contact has confirmed the batch is right
Only when the contact has sent you a complaint

knowledgeChecks.question: A clinic manager wants to publish a review with her name and a photo of the cleaned trolleys. What do you need?
options: Her consent for the name and photo you plan to publish
Nothing, because the review is positive
Your own judgement that the photo looks professional

knowledgeChecks.question: What should a referral reward look like?
options: Paid to anyone who mentions your name
Decided after the referred person books, based on how keen the referrer seems
Decided and written in advance, with the condition for payment stated

knowledgeChecks.question: When does the lesson say to propose the next step for the contact?
options: At the end of each job, with a date
